title: DMYCC

description.main: A decade-long photographic record of an abandoned Second Avenue Subway tunnel segment beneath Lower Manhattan.
description.extended:
A decade-long photographic record of a disused Second Avenue Subway tunnel segment beneath Lower Manhattan, which Sean Vegezzi and friends turned into a private social and working space.

The New York City Transit Authority built the tunnel in the 1970s, and it was then neglected. DMYCC is an initialism covering the space itself, the wish to get into it and the changing efforts to set up a private recreational domain there. The 624 pages follow a loose chronology, from early analogue photographs through video stills, receipts and architectural floor plans to full-scale photographic surveys of the space. Vegezzi also turns surveillance methods back on the authorities and other intruders. The softback has a faux-leather cover.

Vegezzi (b. 1990) works in image-making, sculpture, writing and spatial intervention. Their first book of photographs was IDWGU (Fourteen-Nineteen, 2012), a narrative of adolescence in Lower Manhattan, followed by Snow Cab (Loose Joints, 2016).
